title: Sell Mineral Rights in Starkville, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Starkville, CO | Raton Basin CBM
metaDescription: Starkville sits in the Raton Basin coalbed methane trend near Trinidad, with a coal mining history layered under it. Get an honest offer on your Las Animas interest.
heroLead: Starkville was a coal camp before it was anything else, and that coal history still shapes what a mineral interest here actually means.
intro: Just south of Trinidad, Starkville grew up around the coal seams that later became the source rock for Raton Basin coalbed methane production. Selling minerals here means understanding both estates: the coal that was mined out generations ago and the methane gas produced from what's left in the ground.
Starkville's old coal-camp lots were platted small, so a single modern mineral interest here can represent several original town lots consolidated over generations of inheritance.
Because Starkville's population is so small today, most of the mineral interests we see here belong to owners who left the area generations ago and simply held onto the family paper.

sections.heading: Coal estate versus oil and gas estate
paragraphs: In much of Las Animas County, the coal estate and the oil and gas estate were severed separately, sometimes at different points in history and to different parties. That matters because coalbed methane is gas produced from the coal seam itself, which historically created disputes over who controlled drainage rights when coal and CBM ownership didn't match. Before we value your interest, we confirm which estate you actually hold, coal, oil and gas, or both.

sections.heading: A mature, lower-activity CBM basin
paragraphs: Raton Basin CBM drilling in this part of Las Animas County peaked years ago, and well counts here are far lower than in the DJ Basin. Many legacy wells around Starkville are shut in or producing at stripper rates, so we price based on the actual production and decline history tied to your specific unit rather than assuming basin-wide activity.

faqs.question: Do I own the coal, the gas, or both under my Starkville property?
faqs.answer: It depends on how the estate was severed historically. We check the Las Animas County record to confirm exactly what you hold.

faqs.question: Is Raton Basin CBM still active around Starkville?
faqs.answer: Activity has slowed significantly from its peak, and many wells here are mature or shut in, which we factor into any offer.

faqs.question: What records do you need to make an offer?
faqs.answer: Your mineral deed or a legal description, plus any lease or division order paperwork, which we verify through the county clerk and recorder.

faqs.question: Is Starkville close enough to Trinidad to share its production history?
faqs.answer: Yes, Starkville sits within the same Raton Basin district as Trinidad, though well density immediately around Starkville itself has always been lighter than the county seat's core.

faqs.question: Do I need to live in Colorado to sell a Starkville mineral interest?
faqs.answer: No, most of our Starkville sellers live out of state. We handle the county title work and paperwork remotely and close by mail.
